_comment: Places to buy one specific thing. No menu: walk up, the game's own prompt appears
top left, press the key, eat it.
item        an id from foods.json. That is where the price and the hunger live.
label       what the prompt calls it. Defaults to the item's name.
x, y, z     where it is. z is the GROUND; anything spawned is placed on the
ground properly, so being a little out is harmless.
heading     which way a spawned stand faces, 0-360.
reach       how close you have to be to buy, in metres.
item        one id, a list of ids, or a list of { id, from, to } with hours.
An entry with no hours is on the board all day and is what a shop
falls back to. That is how the diner serves breakfast 5-11 and a
plate the rest of the time. Several available at once = random.
fromVehicle true lets you order without getting out -- a drive-through. The
car has to be nearly stopped, and reach wants to be bigger,
because you are measured from the driver seat.
spawnRange  how close before anything is created at all.
hours       open and close, as hours of the day. Outside them the WHOLE pitch
is gone -- a cart standing there all night that cannot be bought
from looks broken, not closed. Omit for always open.
smoke       everyHours is GAME hours between cigarettes; seconds is REAL
seconds spent on one. Each unit measures what it should: how often
he goes is his working day, how long you watch him is watching.
back is how far behind his post he wanders. He will not serve
while he is away.
prop / ped  OPTIONAL candidate lists. Leave them out entirely for a place that
already exists in the world -- a serving hatch, a restaurant door --
and nothing is spawned; it becomes just a spot with a price.
Where they ARE given, the first model that exists in your build wins
and every miss is named in BareMinimum.log.
blipSprite  52 is Store, the shopping bag. CHECK ANY NUMBER YOU PUT HERE: a
sprite the game does not have draws the default dot rather than
nothing, and a wrong one draws the WRONG icon -- 267 is Property
Management and 106 is the FIB, both of which look deliberate.
To add your own: stand where you want it, read the coordinates off a coord HUD,
and copy a block below.
ui        show the shelf menu. ONLY where there is somebody to order from:
a shop you walk into with a cashier. A door on the street gets the
one-key prompt and one item instead.
discount  what fraction of the marked price this place charges. 1 is normal.

_rooms: The game's own interiors a bar's door can put you inside. A door names one by key
with "inside" on the vendor. Every coordinate here is a GUESS the game is asked about
before anybody is moved (GET_INTERIOR_AT_COORDS, free, any point on the map); the
anchor is tried first, then each of "also", and the first with a room in it wins. If
none has, he comes straight back out to the door and the log says which number is off.
tequilala  Rockstar's own probe coordinate for v_rockclub, out of the decompiled
building_controller, with that script's alternate probe and the MLO
origin as fallbacks. In the story map; no IPL, no map swap.
bahama     Bahama Mamas West. Two published coordinates thirty metres apart in Y,
which is the length of the floor, so both are here. Story map, no IPL.
online: true would switch the map to the ONLINE one while he is inside and back on
the way out, for a nightclub or the casino bar. Neither of these needs it.

_groups: The map groups. The pause map's legend collects blips by their distinct name and pages through each name's blips with left and right, so a group IS a shared name -- see [Map] GroupShopBlips, which turns the whole thing off and gives every shop its own name back. A vendor with no group, or one naming a group that is not here, falls back to [Map] ShopBlipGroupName. A vendor with a room behind it ("inside") overrides the group's sprite with 267, the house mark, so the shape says you can walk in and the colour still says what it sells.

_comment: Doors surveyed in game and NOT YET BUILT. The loader reads "vendors" and nothing
else, so everything in here is inert -- a notebook, not a disabled entry.
What is left is the doors that need FOOD WRITTEN FOR THEM: a seafood diner needs
seafood, with a price, a hunger figure, a verified prop and a line about itself.
The branches of shops that already had a menu have been built and removed.
Two Fresh Fruit & Veg stands stay listed for the record and should NOT be built as
vendors -- the roadside stalls are found by model now, so those two are already
working along with every other one in the world.
